items.stem:
Gauri, a shareholder of Nair Industries Ltd, finds that profit rose by ₹20 lakh this year but cannot tell whether this is good, because revenue doubled and the company issued new shares.
(i) What kind of analysis will help Gauri? Why? (ii) State two limitations Gauri should keep in mind.
items.answer: (i) Analysis using ratios and comparative statements, because absolute figures alone do not show relative performance. (ii) Price-level changes are ignored; window dressing and differences in accounting policies may distort results.

items.stem: Explain the following objectives of analysis of financial statements: (i) To assess the short-term and long-term solvency (ii) To forecast and prepare budgets.
items.answer: (i) To assess the short-term and long-term solvency: Ability to pay current and long-term obligations is judged. (ii) To forecast and prepare budgets: Past trends help in planning.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Ability to pay current and long-term obligations is judged. (ii) Past trends help in planning.

Nandini, a shareholder of Agarwal Brothers Ltd, finds that profit rose by ₹20 lakh this year but cannot tell whether this is good, because revenue doubled and the company issued new shares.
(i) What kind of analysis will help Nandini? Why? (ii) State two limitations Nandini should keep in mind.
items.answer: (i) Analysis using ratios and comparative statements, because absolute figures alone do not show relative performance. (ii) Price-level changes are ignored; window dressing and differences in accounting policies may distort results.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Analysis using ratios and comparative statements, because absolute figures alone do not show relative performance. (ii) Price-level changes are ignored; window dressing and differences in accounting policies may distort results.

items.stem: Nikhil places the balance sheets of 2024-25 and 2025-26 side by side and computes the change in each item. Which tool of analysis is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Comparative statements. Two years are compared with absolute and percentage changes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Comparative statements; 2 marks for the justification: Two years are compared with absolute and percentage changes.

items.stem: What is meant by "Comparative balance sheet"?
items.answer: A balance sheet showing the items of two or more dates side by side, with absolute and percentage changes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A balance sheet showing the items of two or more dates side by side, with absolute and percentage changes.

items.stem: Explain the following limitations of financial statement analysis: (i) Ignores price-level changes (ii) Ignores qualitative aspects.
items.answer: (i) Ignores price-level changes: Figures are at historical cost. (ii) Ignores qualitative aspects: Non-monetary factors are not considered.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Figures are at historical cost. (ii) Non-monetary factors are not considered.
